name: Bell Pepper

basicInfo.description: Bell peppers, also known as capsicum, are colorful, sweet, and versatile vegetables. They grow best in warm weather and can be harvested green, yellow, or red depending on maturity.
whyGrow: Adds flavor and color to many dishes
Rich in Vitamin C and antioxidants
Can be eaten raw, roasted, or cooked
One plant produces multiple peppers across the season
basicInfo.water: Keep soil consistently moist, avoid waterlogging

growingSteps: Start seeds indoors 6–8 weeks before the last frost date
Transplant seedlings outdoors when temperatures stay above 18°C
Plant in rich, well-draining soil with compost
Water regularly and mulch to keep soil moist
Stake plants if heavy with fruit
Harvest when peppers reach desired color and size

careCalendar.description: Start seeds in seed trays with warm, moist soil.
Move seedlings to garden beds after frost risk is gone.
Add mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
Apply balanced fertilizer to support flowering.
Pick green peppers or let them ripen to red/yellow.

symptoms: White or pale patches on peppers

harvestingGuide: Harvest green bell peppers when firm and full-sized. For sweeter flavor, wait until they turn red, yellow, or orange. Cut with scissors instead of pulling to avoid damaging stems.
estimatedSavings: Growing bell peppers at home can save $80–100 per season, as store-bought peppers are usually $1–3 each.
